title: Catalyst Retail partnership scratchpad
content:
Quick context: Catalyst Retail = mid-market omnichannel retail platform (CRM + POS + inventory). Potential to bundle Redwood inference for in-store chat assistants, personalized product recommendations, and automated store ops summarization. Heard they pilot other ML vendors but have strict infra/security needs for enterprise customers.

Goals for outreach:
- Get intro with Head of Platform or Director of Data Products
- Land a short discovery to map 2–3 high-impact use cases (store-assist, returns triage, intelligent search)
- Position Redwood as production-first — predictable latency/costs + private deploy options for regulated retail customers

What we know / signals:
- Funding: Series B (2023), growing EMEA footprint
- Tech stack: AWS core, some Azure in EMEA, Postgres + Kafka, React front-end; likely already using SageMaker for experiments (internal notes from job listing)
- Pain: store-level inference is inconsistent; mobile apps complain about latency; pilots stalled on infra ops complexity

Key personas to target:
- Head of Platform: cares about ops, SLAs, integrations (KMS, VPC, IaC templates)
- Director of Data Products: cares about model quality, evaluation, A/B testing, cost/throughput tradeoffs
- Head of Stores / Ops: cares about reliability in stores (low bandwidth), edge/offline modes
- Procurement/Security: privacy, SOC2, KMS/HSM, audit logs

Elevator (1‑liner tailored):
"Catalyst teams can add high-quality conversational assistants and real-time product recommendations without building and operating GPU infra — Redwood gives predictable latency, per-route cost insights, and private deployment options for regulated retail customers."

Outbound subject lines to A/B test:
- "Question about reducing inference latency for in-store assistants"
- "How Catalyst could serve AI features reliably across 300+ stores"
- "Pilot idea: conversational returns triage — low ops, measurable ROI"

LinkedIn intro (short):
Hi [Name],
I’m Maya — I lead partnerships at Redwood Inference. We help teams ship LLM features with predictable latency/cost and private deployment options for regulated customers. I’d love to share a short pilot idea that’s working for other retailers — 10 minutes?

Voicemail script (20s):
Hi [Name], it’s Maya from Redwood Inference. We help retail platforms run production LLMs with predictable latency and lower token costs. I have an idea for a small pilot that could reduce returns handling time by ~30% without adding infra. Can I grab 15 minutes next week? My number is 415‑555‑0123.

Cold email (short):
Subject: Pilot idea to cut in-store assistant latency
Hi [Name],
We’ve helped retailers move from experimental LLM integrations to production by reducing median inference latency from 700ms to ~120ms and dropping per-query cost via batching/caching. If you’re open, I’d love to share a 15‑minute pilot plan for Catalyst that keeps data in your VPC and gives measurable KPIs (latency, cost, deflection).
Thanks,
Maya

Discovery questions (to surface needs):
- Which product/feature teams are owning conversational/search features today?
- What does your current inference stack look like in production? Any pods/endpoints?
- Typical latency targets for user-facing flows (web vs mobile vs in-store devices)?
- Volume: tokens/requests per minute at peak and off-peak?
- Data residency/compliance constraints? Any customers requiring on-prem or air-gapped deployments?
- How do you measure feature ROI today? (conversion, AOV, handle time)

Objections & suggested responses (quick bullets):
1) "We already use vendor X / managed cloud"
   - Response: Many teams start there; Redwood complements model access with a production runtime — predictable SLOs, cost controls, and private deployments (VPC + on-prem) so you can avoid building edge infra. Offer a 2‑week POC comparing latency/cost.
2) "Security / compliance concerns"
   - Response: Redwood Private supports customer-managed control plane, KMS/HSM integrations, SOC2-ready logs, audit trails. Offer doc pack + architecture patterns for VPC and HSM.
3) "Too expensive / token costs"
   - Response: We optimize cost with caching, batching, and quantization guidance. For retail search, prefix caching and KV reuse often reduce token compute by 40–60% — show sample calc + sample bill comparison.
4) "We need model customization / brand voice"
   - Response: We support model versioning, safe fine-tune/adapter workflows, and evaluation harnesses tied to your prompt sets so quality regressions are detectable pre-rollout.

Pilot idea (4–6 week):
Goal: Replace current returns triage heuristic with an LLM-based assistant to auto-suggest resolutions and pre-fill claims.
- Week 0: kickoff + access (API keys, test VPC)
- Week 1: narrow prompt set + baseline metrics (current handle time, deflection)
- Week 2–3: model variant A/B test (hosted vs dedicated) + latency profiling
- Week 4: integrate with web hooks + small in-store rollout in 2 pilot stores
Success metrics: 30% reduction in avg handling time, 15% more self-serve resolutions, median latency <200ms for store devices

Technical notes for internal follow-up:
- Ask infra: can they expose ephemeral private endpoint to integrate with Redwood Private? (RDW-2345 follow-up)
- Security wants: encryption in transit + at rest, HSM for keys, audit logs retention 1 year minimum
- Bandwidth constraints in stores: propose edge routing to nearest region + smaller model variant with quantization for devices

Playbook snippets (for SDR):
- If they say "pilot budget", pivot to pilot sprint: low-cost POC with measurable metrics; estimate engineering time 2 weeks + data ingest 1 week.
- If they ask for reference, use retailer X (anonymized success) — provide latency and cost delta numbers + short case study link.

Open items / TODOs:
- [ ] Prep one-pager tailored to returns triage + cost comparison (owner: Priya)
- [ ] Get security architecture template for VPC/HSM (owner: Ethan)
- [ ] Create short demo script + prompts for in-store device (owner: Maya)
- [ ] Draft contract language for pilot data handling (legal)

Notes to self: keep outreach lightweight. Prioritize Head of Platform and Data Products over Ops for first intro. Use warm ref if we can get an intro from mutual VC or partner.

Meeting agenda (15 min discovery):
- 0–2m: intros and context
- 2–6m: quick current state (inference stack, pain points)
- 6–10m: pilot idea + success metrics
- 10–13m: security/ops callouts
- 13–15m: next steps (POC scope, timeline, stakeholders)

Slack notes (for outreach channel):
@Priya — I’ll ping Catalyst Head of Platform (LinkedIn) today. If we get a reply, can you slot 30m next week (tech + security)?

Random brainstorm lines (do not use in first email):
- "Embedded checkout hints" for upsell via conversation history
- "Returns clustering" to automatically generate return reason taxonomy by store
- "SKU similarity embeddings" for smarter recommendations at register

End of scratchpad — save as working draft.
